findings.body: Ownership is recorded only after `_new_checkout` returns, but that helper creates the worktree at `src/forge/task.py:116` and commits its record at line 122 through `repo.commit_state` (`src/forge/repo.py:494`). If a hook rejects this first commit, `created` remains false although this invocation created the folder and branch. The handler at lines 277–279 then treats them as another run's fix: it skips cleanup and replaces the rejection reason with the finish-or-remove step. This leaves an unlocked, incomplete checkout behind, contrary to item 4. This failure boundary is new evidence beyond the overlapping-run race already fixed. Record ownership immediately after successful worktree creation while retaining protection for competing runs. Extend the command-level refusal test: its hook currently rejects only the later files commit (`tests/test_doctor_fix_files.py:396`).
findings.title: Not done: failed commits clean up the new fix and show the reason

findings.body: The empty-fix path ignores `_drop`'s result. If the new worktree cannot be removed—for example, its successful record-commit hook locks it—doctor returns only `held`, potentially reporting success while leaving its folder and branch behind. The link-refusal path at line 268 likewise ignores cleanup failure and omits the leftover folder from its message. Check both results and report the remaining folder when removal fails.
findings.title: Report cleanup failures when discarding a new fix
